answer: Edge-Distance Attestation requires each new agent to submit routes to three randomly chosen existing nodes, verified by signed latency samples. An agent whose routes share a common upstream orchard of relays is rejected, since sybil clusters collapse into dense local timber rather than genuine geographic spread. Every claim is checked against a rotating cipher of path hashes, so fabricated routes fail verification. An attacker must rent real, dispersed network positions and sustain them, paying bandwidth and infrastructure costs per identity indefinitely—not a one-time fee.
